title: Life Manager: A Manager You Do Not Have to Prompt Every Day
markdown:
# Life Manager: A Manager You Do Not Have to Prompt Every Day

Most software waits. You open it, you type what to do, and nothing moves until you ask again. Life Manager is described on its product page in the opposite way: one proactive manager for work, money, everyday responsibilities, body, and mind, that chooses useful priorities, carries work forward, and verifies outcomes, including income-generating work, without a daily prompt.

## What "no daily prompt" actually means here

The product page states it plainly: no daily instructions or user-defined goals and budgets are required by the product design. Its operating requirement is called No Human in the Loop: registration, publication, distribution, and reconciliation are meant to run on agent-owned work accounts, without daily prompts, approval chats, or your private service credentials.

That is a design requirement, stated honestly. The page also says intervention-free registration, publication, and payment are still being verified end to end, and positive net returns are not verified yet. No daily prompting is the way it is built to run, not a promise that every path is already finished.

## What it manages, in its own three areas

Money and business: find work, create and sell, and track income and spending, with attempted actions distinguished from verified payments.

Work and everyday life: goals, priorities, schedules, applications, and follow-ups, moving delegated work forward and verifying the outcome.

Body and mind: routines, daily rhythms, and well-being, brought into the same system that manages the rest of your life, instead of a separate app you have to prompt separately.

Calendar travel-time planning is one workflow in that system. The page is explicit that it is not the product.

## How earning work keeps moving

The page names the earning loops MoneyPrinter, and lists their steps in order: find opportunities such as gigs, jobs, and customers; create and apply within delegated boundaries; distribute by selling, submitting, and publishing; verify results with completion and payment evidence; then improve by reviewing costs and outcomes.

Its economic acceptance criterion is also stated on the page: earning more than your subscription fee and all operating costs. The page adds, in the same place, that positive net returns are not verified yet, capabilities depend on integrations and setup, and income and investment returns are not guaranteed.

## How it starts

Run the same open-source core locally, or use the hosted mode from your phone on a dedicated Maritime VM. Start with Google identity only; signup does not require Calendar or Gmail inbox access, a task prompt, goals, budget, or payout details. Progress and verified results are designed to go to your sign-in email.

The first hosted earning workflow is being connected to Capafy. Capafy requires Publisher Certification and publisher confirmation of selected Skills and configuration before each Agent version can go live, and Life Manager reports listings and earnings only after Capafy confirms them.

Pricing, stated plainly: $29/month after a 7-day free trial. Price on the site: 29 USD.

If you are tired of software that only moves when you prompt it, start from the product page, where the no-daily-prompt design, its current limits, and the price are all stated in one place:

- Life Manager: https://aniccaai.com/lm

One manager for your whole life.
